ap_macroeconomics-m01.stem: During a recession, which of the following happens automatically, without any new legislation?

options.text: The central bank raises the required reserve ratio.
options.why: Monetary policy requires a decision by the central bank and is not a fiscal stabilizer.

options.text: Tax revenues rise and transfer payments fall, which reduces aggregate demand further.
options.why: Reverses the direction of the automatic changes.

options.text: Tax revenues fall and transfer payments rise, which reduces the decline in aggregate demand.
options.why: A progressive tax system and transfers act as automatic stabilizers.

options.text: The budget balance moves toward a surplus.
options.why: A recession moves the budget toward a deficit.

options.text: Government purchases rise by an act of Congress.
options.why: Requires new legislation, so it is discretionary.

ap_macroeconomics-m01.stem: Which of the following is an example of an automatic stabilizer?

options.text: A new law raises the minimum wage.
options.why: Not a mechanism that automatically offsets changes in output.

options.text: Congress passes a law to increase spending on highways during a recession.
options.why: A new law is discretionary fiscal policy, not an automatic stabilizer.

options.text: The government cuts tax rates by new legislation during a recession.
options.why: A legislated tax cut is discretionary fiscal policy.

options.text: The central bank buys bonds in the open market.
options.why: Open market operations are monetary policy, not a built-in fiscal stabilizer.

options.text: Unemployment benefits that rise when more people lose their jobs.
options.why: Transfer payments rise automatically in a downturn without new legislation, cushioning the fall in disposable income.
